name: Omnitech Engineering Ltd
tagline: Recently-listed small-cap precision-engineered components (machining/forging/casting) exporter riding a ~970% order-book surge (energy-heavy) into a big FY27/28 capacity expansion - genuinely strong growth, but still ~66x trailing P/E / ~10x book with a QoQ margin wobble in its first post-listing quarter.
business_overview: Omnitech Engineering manufactures high-precision engineered components and assemblies (machining, grinding, turning, sub-assembly across carbon/alloy/stainless steel, nickel alloys, titanium, aluminium) for 256+ customers across ~24 countries, serving energy (oil & gas, wind, power - now 73.7% of the order book), motion-control/automation, and industrial-equipment end markets; North America is ~53% of revenue and ~75% of revenue is international. Listed on NSE/BSE on 5 March 2026. NOTE: a separate, unrelated listed entity, Omnitech Infosolutions Ltd (an IT services micro-cap, market cap ~Rs 1.6 Cr, negative ROE/ROCE), also trades under a similar name - this write-up is for Omnitech Engineering Ltd (NSE: OMNI), the entity judged the far more plausible match for the bullish X mention given Infosolutions' distressed/dormant state; this identification is not 100% certain and should be re-confirmed if used for a serious position. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@ParthaAwe, bullish/medium conviction, 2026-09-13).
fundamentals_table: FY24 ~Rs178cr -> FY25 ~Rs343-350cr (+92%) -> FY26 consol ~Rs511cr (+49.1%) -> Q1FY27 (Jun-26) consol ~Rs167cr (+61.5% YoY)
~Rs 3,033 Cr as of May-26, up from ~Rs 284 Cr a year earlier (~970% YoY); Energy 73.7% / Motion-control&automation 13.7% / Industrial equipment 12.6%
~0.7x post-IPO (~Rs435cr debt vs ~Rs680cr equity, Jun-26) - down from ~1.6-1.72x pre-IPO (FY25) as IPO proceeds + retained earnings built equity
Debtor days ~153-172; cash-conversion-cycle reported elongating (~61 to ~180 days) over the growth ramp - a real cash-drag flag

Rs ~235cr FY23-25 (machines 161->247->292, capacity commercialised H1FY25); new Rs ~250cr FY27 (Rs100cr building + Rs150cr plant&machinery, spillover to FY28) targeting ~42-43 lakh annualised machine-hours vs ~26.4 lakh now
fundamentals_narrative: Omnitech Engineering is a genuine, and now accelerating, growth story: revenue nearly doubled FY24-FY25 (~Rs178cr to ~Rs343cr), grew a further ~49% in FY26 (~Rs511cr), and Q1 FY27 (Jun-26, first full quarter as a listed company) grew consolidated revenue +61.5% YoY with standalone PAT up 468.7% YoY (off a low base) to ~Rs29.7cr. The real new development this pass is the order book: it jumped ~970% YoY to ~Rs3,033cr by May-26 (vs ~Rs284cr a year earlier), heavily concentrated in energy (73.7%), backing a fresh ~Rs250cr capacity-expansion programme (FY27, spillover FY28) that would take machine-hour capacity up ~60%. Management called Q1FY27 'disciplined margin management' and a 'meaningful reduction in working-capital days', but the sequential numbers show EBITDA grew only ~1% QoQ (Rs50cr to Rs50.6cr) on ~12% QoQ revenue growth (Rs149cr to Rs167cr) - the promised operating leverage has not yet shown up in a single quarter's print, and working-capital metrics (debtor days ~153-172, a cash-conversion-cycle that widened over the ramp) remain a genuine caution alongside real leverage improvement post-IPO (D/E ~1.6-1.72x pre-IPO down to ~0.7x). Valuation has partially de-rated on the earnings catch-up (P/E ~84x -> ~66-68x) but at ~10x book and ~66x trailing earnings there is still very little margin of safety for a business whose next leg (the new capacity, and conversion of a heavily energy-concentrated order book) is entirely unproven as a public company. Promoter pledge status and related-party-transaction specifics could not be independently confirmed this pass (a CARE Ratings PDF fetch failed and no other source carried the detail) - flagged as an open question, not assumed clean.

Strong, broad-based revenue growth (~92% FY25, +49% FY26, +61.5% YoY Q1FY27) across a 256+ customer, 24-country base - plausible China+1/supply-chain-diversification beneficiary, now moving up the value chain into aerospace (AS9100:2015 certification + 4 First-Article development orders)

Working capital has elongated through the growth ramp (debtor days ~153-172, cash-conversion cycle reportedly widening ~61 to ~180 days) - classic cash-drag-from-growth risk

verdict_headline: Genuinely accelerating precision-components exporter with a ~970% order-book surge behind it, but four_box score still 2.5 (valuation remains a hard 'no' at ~66-68x P/E / ~10x book, and Q1FY27's flat-QoQ EBITDA shows the operating leverage isn't proven yet) - 'neither', conviction held at Medium.
verdict_reasoning: four_box = 2.5 (tailwind yes - the order book explosion confirms real, not just narrative, energy-sector demand; tam yes - broad 24-country, 256+ customer base, order book ~44% of market cap; moat weak - AS9100 aerospace certification and 5-micron tolerances help but this remains a competitive machining/forging space; valuation no - ~66-68x P/E and ~10x book leave no margin of safety even after the recent earnings-driven de-rating from ~84x).

Score stays in the 2.0-2.5 band -> defaults to 'neither'. Considered invoking the 'growth is un-ignorable' carve-out given the order-book surge, but declined: the same order book concentrates single-point-of-failure risk in one sector against an unbuilt ~Rs250cr capacity expansion, and Q1FY27's ~1% QoQ EBITDA growth on ~12% QoQ revenue growth is a live data point that the promised operating leverage has not yet arrived - the carve-out is for un-ignorable growth, not for a still-unproven execution thesis riding a rich multiple.

Conviction held at Medium (unchanged from pre-dive): the order-book/growth news is genuinely bullish and new this pass, but it is offset by the QoQ margin wobble, elongating working capital, and an unresolved promoter-pledge/RPT open question - net roughly a wash versus the pre-dive read.
Entity identification (Omnitech Engineering Ltd vs. the unrelated micro-cap Omnitech Infosolutions Ltd) is reasonably but not fully confident - flagged explicitly for re-confirmation.
